. The petitioner herein has filed the instant petition for grant of bail in case titled as "UT of J&K Vs.
Hakim Hussain" pending trial before the court of learned Sessions Judge, Poonch (for short the 'trial court') arising out of FIR No. 364/2022 dated 05.12.2022 for offences under Sections 376/456/506 IPC.

According to the prosecution version, the complainant/respondent 3 herein lodged a complaint before the Police Station, Surankote stating therein that she was knowing the accused/petitioner herein being a tailor by profession running a tailoring shop in the close vicinity of the residential quarter wherein the complainant/respondent 3 herein was putting up along with her husband and two minor children and was also getting her clothes stitched by him and that in the month of January 2021, the accused petitioner herein came to her residential quarter and sought permission to perform ablution for offering prayers, whereafter doing the same, the accused petitioner herein left her residential quarter, however, came back after 10/15 minutes and told her that he has forgotten his mobile phone therein the bathroom and that upon being permitted to take back the same, the accused/petitioner herein took his mobile phone back and that after 4/5 days, the accused/petitioner herein called her at his shop and showed her a video of her from his phone and threatened her that he had infact filmed the complainant/respondent 3 herein through his mobile phone, when he had deliberately kept the same in her bathroom and that thereafter the Hakim Hussain vs Ut Of J&K And Another on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114087717/
1 accused/petitioner herein compelled her to agree to wrongs committed by him on her and that the complainant/respondent 3 herein continuously requested and begged the accused/petitioner herein not to do wrong things with her, yet her said request did not yield any result and the accused/petitioner herein continued to exploit the complainant/respondent 3 herein sexually and that on 19.12.2021, the husband of the complainant/respondent 3 herein had gone to Jammu in connection with his work and that she was alone with her minor children in the residential quarter and in the evening after making her children to go to sleep, the accused/petitioner with an ill intention came to her residential quarter and after threatening her, committed rape upon her against her will as also gave her a beating besides tearing her shirt and also locked her minor daughter in the bathroom, as she woke up from sleep on account of the noise of her beating and that after raping her the accused/petitioner herein threatened her that if she reveals the act to anyone, he will kill her and that otherwise also nobody is going to trust her as she has been converted upon her marriage and that, as such, the complainant/respondent 3 herein owing to those threats did not reveal the acts of rape either to her husband or to anyone else in the family and instead insisted her husband to shift from the residential quarter to the newly constructed house, however, even after shifting in the newly constructed residential house, the accused/petitioner herein continued to commit rape upon the complainant/respondent 3 herein against her will and that upon finding no way out, the complainant/respondent 3 herein revealed the incidents to her husband and brother of her husband and consequently got the FIR registered against the accused/petitioner herein.

It is further version of the prosecution that upon registration of the FIR, investigation came to be undertaken and upon completion of the investigation, the offences alleged in the complaint by the complainant/respondent 3 against the accused/petitioner herein got established and consequently charge-sheet was laid before the trial court.
3. The accused/petitioner herein has maintained the instant petition before this Court being his second attempt for seeking bail in the aforesaid case pending trial before the trial court, wherein the accused/petitioner herein have had in his first attempt maintained the bail application earlier on 02.11.2023, which however came to be rejected by the trial court on 30.11.2023.
4. The accused/petitioner herein while maintaining the instant petition before this Court has urged following grounds for seeking concession of bail:-
(a) That the challan in the said FIR is pending since more than one year against the petitioner herein and he is under arrest since 05.11.2022 and the prosecution has examined only three witnesses during the pendency of the challan and the prime witnesses i.e. the prosecutrix, her husband and her daughter has been examined by the prosecution and there are major discrepancies in the statements of all in cross examination they have not supported the prosecution story.

(b) That the petitioner is in the custody of the police since more than one year and if with the same pace the trial will continue it will take years together for the petitioner to face the trial before the court below and the custody of the petitioner is an abuse of process of law as he has been treated as a convicted person whereas the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that a person is presumed to be innocent person unless and until he is Hakim Hussain vs Ut Of J&K And Another on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114087717/
2 convicted.
(c) That the trial court while dismissing the bail application has held that there is a apprehension of tempering of the prime witnesses by the petitioner herein, whereas the court below i.e. trial court has overlooked the aspect of the case that the prime witness has already been examined in the case and the only official witness which are to be examined by the prosecution now and the custody of the petitioner is illegal on the aspect that he is presently facing a trial and he is not a convicted person and he is only of 45 years of age and the family of the petitioner i.e. his three children and wife are at the verge of starvation as the petitioner was the only source of income for the dependents.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Moreover, the old parents of the petitioner are also at the verge of starvation and if the bail is not granted to the petitioner at this stage, then not only the petitioner but whole family which includes the children, mother, wife and father of the petitioner will have to face the starvation.

(d) That the trial court while rejecting the bail application of the petitioner has held that the nature of the accusation and severity of the punishment in case of conviction and nature of supporting evidence is to be taken into account.

Whereas the law is well settled that the nature of the offences is and the severity of the punishment is only to be looked at the final stage of the hearing after going through the evidence, but at this initial stage of the challan once the petitioner is facing the trial for more than one year when only three witnesses those are the prime witnesses have already been examined by the prosecution and rest of the witnesses are only the official witnesses and the question of tempering the official witnesses cannot be taken into account as they all are police witnesses.
So, the petitioner on this solitary ground as well is entitled for the grant of bail.
(e) That while granting the bail, the court below have not to look into the merits of the evidence and not to comment upon the evidence lead by the prosecution as well as by the defence side.

That only it is the discretion of the judge and the court while granting the bail to look into the stage of case and how much time it will take for final disposal of the case and in the present case already more than one year has been taken by prosecution and the only three witnesses has been examined.
So, the petitioner is entitled for grant of bail at this stage as well.

(f) That even if we go by the evidence lead by the prosecution fill so far in the cross examination all the witnesses have not supported the prosecution witnesses and there are major discrepancies in their statements and on this ground as well the petitioner is entitled for the bail at this stage.

(g) That the court below has dismissed the bail application by giving reason of apprehension on the part of the accused for tempering the witnesses, whereas in the present case now the official witnesses which are:- one is the witness of arrest memo and another is IO so the question of tempering these witnesses cannot be looked into or it is of the domain of the petitioner who is a tailor by profession to temper a police witnesses.

So, on this analogy as well the finding of the court Hakim Hussain vs Ut Of J&K And Another on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114087717/
3 below while rejecting the bail application is illegal and the petitioner herein is entitled for the grant of bail.

sentences.text: (h) That even in the interest of justice and the propriety demands that a person is to be treated as innocent unless and until he is convicted and in the present case the accused is facing trial which has already mentioned above for more than one year and he is behind bars, so his liberty has been stalled by all these proceedings which is to be finally been disposed off when the challan is to be finally being heard and it will take years together for the final disposal of the case.

So, in order to put the petitioner on the liberty he should be granted bail at this stage and even the Hon'ble Apex Court has held in various judgments that a person should be granted bail while facing trial.

5. Objections to the petition have been filed by the official respondents, wherein the same is being opposed, inter alia, on the premise that the accused/petitioner herein is involved in the commission of heinous offence of rape being not only against the victim, but also against the State/Society and that since charge-sheet has been laid before the trial court, some of the witnesses therein have also been examined, which witnesses have supported the case of the prosecution and that in the event the accused/petitioner is granted concession of bail by this Court, the same shall have an adverse effect on the trial of the case and that the accused/petitioner herein may also get encouraged and also may jump over the bail.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
6. It is significant to mention here that according to the appearing counsel for the parties, out of seven listed witnesses up till now four witnesses have been examined by the trial court.

7. Before adverting to the rival submissions of the appearing counsel for the parties made by them in line with their respective pleadings, it would be appropriate to refer to the position of law laid down by the Apex Court on the subject of bail and issues connected thereto.

The Apex Court in case titled as "Anil Kumar Yadav vs. State (NCT of Delhi)" reported in 2018 (12) SCC 129 has laid down at paras 15, 17 and 18 as follows:
"15.

entities.text: Anil Kumar Yadav vs. State (NCT of Delhi)" reported in 2018 (12) SCC 129
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As held in Puran case [2001(6) SCC 338], while considering the question of grant of bail, court should avoid consideration of details of evidence as it is not a relevant consideration.
While it is necessary to consider the prima facie case, an exhaustive exploration of the merits of the case should be avoided.
We, therefore, consciously refrain from considering the merits of the consciously refrain from considering the merits of the materials/ evidence collected by the prosecution."

"17. While granting bail, the relevant considerations are:-
(i) nature of seriousness of the offence; (ii) character of the evidence and circumstances which are peculiar to the accused; and (iii) likelihood of the accused fleeing from justice; (iv) the impact that his release may make on the prosecution witnesses, its impact on the society; and (v) likelihood of his tampering.

No doubt,

4

There are no hard and fast rules regarding grant or refusal of bail, each case has to be considered on its own merits.
The matter always calls for judicious exercise of discretion by the Court."

While considering the basic requirement of the grant of bail, in "State of UP Th. CBI vs. Amarmani Tripathi", this Court has held as under:-
"18.

entities.text: State of UP Th. CBI vs. Amarmani Tripathi
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is well settled that the matters to be considered in an application for bail are (i) whether there is any prima facie or reasonable ground to believe that the accused had committed the offence; (ii)
nature and gravity of the charge; (iii) severity of the punishment in the event of conviction; (iv)
danger of the accused absconding or fleeing, if released on bail; (v) character, behaviour, means,
position and standing of the accused; (vi) likelihood of the offence being repeated; (vii) reasonable apprehension of the witnesses being tampered with; and (viii) danger, of course, of justice being thwarted by grant of bail [see Prahlad Singh Bhati Vs. NCT,
Delhi and Gurcharan Singh Vs. State (NCT of Delhi)].
8.

In case titled as Neeru Yadav vs. State of Uttar Pradesh and another reported in (2014) 15 SCC 508, the Apex Court at para 16 has held as under:
"16. .........

entities.text: Neeru Yadav vs. State of Uttar Pradesh and another reported in (2014) 15 SCC 508
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: We are not oblivious to the fact that liberty is a priceless treasure for a human.
It is founded on the bedrock of the constitutional right and accentuated further on the human rights principle.
It is basically a natural right.
In fact, some regard it as the grammar of life.
No one would like to lose his liberty or barter it for all the wealth of the world.
People from centuries have fought for liberty, for absence of liberty causes sense of emptiness.
The sanctity of liberty is the fulcrum of any civilised society.
It is a cardinal value on which the civilisation rests.
It cannot be allowed to be paralysed and immobilised.
Deprivation of liberty of a person has enormous impact on his mind as well as body.
A democratic body polity which which is wedded to the rule of law, anxiously guards liberty.
But, a pregnant and significant one, the liberty of an individual is not absolute.

Society by its collective wisdom through process of law can withdraw the liberty that it has sanctioned to an individual when an individual becomes a danger to the collective and to the societal order.
Accent on individual liberty cannot be pyramided to that extent which would bring chaos and anarchy to a society.

A society expects responsibility and accountability from its members, and it desires that the citizens should obey the law,
respecting it as a cherished social norm.
No individual can make an attempt to create a concavity in the stern of social stream.
It is impermissible.
Therefore, when an individual behaves in a disharmonious manner ushering in disorderly things which the society disapproves, the legal consequences are bound to follow.
At that stage, the court has a duty.
It cannot abandon its sacrosanct obligation and pass an order at its own whim or caprice.
It has to be guided by the established parameters of law."

5 9.

sentences.text: Keeping in mind the aforesaid principles of law laid down by the Apex Court and reverting back to the case in hand, perusal of the statement of the complainant/respondent 3 herein made before the trial court as also the statements made by her prior to the filing of the charge-sheet recorded under section 164-A of the Code of Criminal Procedure manifestly reveals the involvement of accused/petitioner herein in the commission of alleged offences, which statements cannot be overlooked or discarded at this stage by this Court on the ground of contradictions pointed out by the counsel for the petitioner herein, more so in view of the fact that no final finding in regard to the statement/s of the complainant/respondent 3 herein can be made by this Court while considering the instant application, in view of the law laid down by the Apex Court in case titled Neeru Yadav (Supra), wherein touching the merits of the case while considering the application for bail has been forbidden, besides undertaking detailed examination of the evidence and elaborate documentation of the merits of the case, as in law, while considering a bail application it is equally settled that the court has to make a prima facie opinion on the basis of the material available before it and also to take into consideration heavily the nature of the accusation and severity of punishment in case of conviction and the nature of the accusation besides the reasonable apprehension of tamper with witness or apprehension of threat to the complainant and lastly the prima facie satisfaction of the court in support of the charge.

Here it needs to be pointed out that having regard to the plea raised by the counsel for the accused/petitioner herein that the alleged occurrence of rape has been reported belatedly by the complainant/respondent 3 herein which per se casts shadow on the allegations of rape levelled by the complainant/respondent 3 herein against the petitioner herein cannot be attached with any importance at this stage in view of the observations made by the Apex Court in case titled as "Wahid Khan vs. State of Madhya Pradesh" reported in (2010) 2 SCC 9 wherein it has been observed as under:
"It is a matter of common law that in Indian society any girl or woman would not make an allegation of rape against a person as she is fully aware of the repercussions flowing therefrom and if she is found to be false, she would be looked by the society with contempt throughout her life."

A further reference to the following observation of the Apex Court made in Neeru Yadav case (Supra) would be appropriate hereunder:-
"...........A democratic body polity which which is wedded to the rule of law, anxiously guards liberty.
But, a pregnant and significant one, the liberty of an individual is not absolute.

Society by its collective wisdom through process of law can withdraw the liberty that it has sanctioned to an individual when an individual becomes a danger to the collective and to the societal order.
Accent on individual liberty cannot be pyramided to that extent which would bring chaos and anarchy to a society.
A society expects responsibility and accountability from its members, and it desires that the citizens should obey the law, respecting it as a cherished social norm.
No individual can make an attempt to create a concavity in the stern of social stream.
It is impermissible.

Therefore, when an individual behaves in a disharmonious manner Hakim Hussain vs Ut Of J&K And Another on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114087717/
6 ushering in disorderly things which the society disapproves, the legal consequences are bound to follow.

It cannot abandon its sacrosanct obligation and pass an order at its own whim or caprice.

It has to be guided by the established parameters of law".
10.

Viewed thus, what has been observed, considered and analysed hereinabove, inasmuch as the facts and circumstances obtaining in the matter, the prosecution version against the petitioner in particular the evidence having come up before the trial court, inasmuch as the principles of law laid down by the Apex Court in the judgments (Supra), the accused/petitioner herein is not found to be entitled to the concession of bail at this stage.
11. The petition accordingly is dismissed.

However, it is made clear that any observation made hereinabove shall not be construed by the trial court to be an expression of any opinion about the guilt or innocence of the accused/petitioner herein as the same will be decided by the trial court on its merits after analysing the evidence that surface on record during the trial of the case.
